issues.issue: Were the removal orders validly made, given who signed them and when the delegate's review happened?
issues.applicant_position: Removal orders were invalid: signed without proper authority, and the delegate's review happened three months later.
issues.respondent_position: Officer Sunger and Acting Chief Leger both had power to sign, so who signed was of no consequence.
issues.result_quote: the Court finds that the tribunal’s conclusion in this regard is both contrary to law and unreasonable

issues.issue: Did the tribunal breach procedural fairness by failing to summon Officer Sunger?
issues.applicant_position: Tribunal should have summoned Officer Sunger to testify on who reviewed the removal orders.
issues.result_quote: it will not be necessary to examine the two other grounds of attack raised by the applicants

issues.issue: Did the tribunal fail to properly assess the best interests of the child?
issues.applicant_position: Tribunal unreasonably failed to properly assess the child's best interests.
issues.respondent_position: Respondent asks the Court to dismiss the application.
issues.result_quote: it will not be necessary to examine the two other grounds of attack raised by the applicants

issues.issue: Should the matter be referred back to the tribunal, or should the removal orders be declared null and void?
issues.applicant_position: Court should simply declare the removal orders illegal and null and void.
issues.respondent_position: Application should be dismissed because the result would be the same.
issues.result_quote: it is proper to make a declaration that the removal orders are null and void
